extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary audience); patent practitioners as secondary audience
extracted.subtask_short: final rejection practice for patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to make, withdraw, and respond to final rejections (and related reissue/previously-allowed-claim practice) in patent examination, including form paragraphs, timing (SSP), advisory actions, examiner amendments, and extension-of-time procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue broadening timing under 35 U.S.C. 251
rubrics_metrics.description: When the reissue is applied for within 2 years (or properly claims the benefit of a broadening reissue application filed within 2 years of the patent grant), the examiner does not go into the question of undue delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reissue broadening is timely (within 2 years or claims benefit of such), undue delay is not examined; otherwise, potential statutory bars may apply. (Context: 35 U.S.C. 251)

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee limitation on filing reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignee of the entire interest may file a reissue application only in cases where it does not 'enlarge the scope of the claims of the original patent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that enlarge scope may be rejected as barred by the statute; however, courts (e.g., In re Bennett) have permitted correction of erroneous filings by assignees in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective reissue oath grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A defective reissue oath affords a ground for rejecting all the claims in the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1444 for detailed treatment; a defective oath is a substantive basis to reject the reissue application claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application special status
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application is 'special' and remains so even if applicant does not make a prompt reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat reissue applications with the 'special' handling ordinarily accorded them; special status persists irrespective of promptness of applicant replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of previously allowed claims requires primary examiner approval
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable shall thereafter be rejected only after the proposed rejection has been submitted to the primary examiner for consideration of all the facts and approval of the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great care should be exercised before authorizing such rejection. Full faith and credit should generally be given to a previous examiner's search and action unless a clear error or knowledge of other prior art exists. Examiners should not take an entirely new approach or make a new search merely hoping to find something. Use Form Paragraph 7.50 to note previously allowed claims now rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.50 — Claims Previously Allowed, Now Rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: The indicated allowability of claim [1] is withdrawn in view of the newly discovered reference(s) to [2]. Rejection(s) based on the newly cited reference(s) follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 insert the name(s) of the newly discovered reference(s). Any action including this form paragraph requires the signature of a Primary Examiner. See MPEP § 1004.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection may be made on second or subsequent examination (37 CFR 1.113)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the second or any subsequent examination or consideration by the examiner the rejection or other action may be made final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When made final, applicant's reply is limited (appeal or restricted amendment routes). The examiner must repeat or state all grounds of rejection then considered applicable and clearly state reasons in support thereof. Reply to a final rejection must include cancellation of, or appeal from, each rejected claim. If any claim stands allowed, reply must comply with requirements or objections as to form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a clear issue before making final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Before final rejection is in order a clear issue should be developed between the examiner and applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search and apply references thoroughly in the first action; applicant should be given opportunity to amend to avoid grounds. Avoid switching subject matter in successive amendments or switching references in successive rejections. Do not sanction hasty or ill-considered final rejections; applicant entitled to full and fair hearing. Applicants who delay or use subterfuges may not avoid final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of grounds required in final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: In making the final rejection, all outstanding grounds of rejection of record should be carefully reviewed and any such grounds relied on in the final rejection should be reiterated and clearly developed so applicant may readily judge the advisability of an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a single previous Office action contains a complete statement supporting the rejection, the final rejection may refer to that statement but should include a rebuttal of any arguments raised in applicant's reply. Examiner's answer on appeal should contain a complete statement of the examiner's position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.39 — Action Is Final (form content & notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph notifying applicant that the action is final and reminding of extension of time policy (37 CFR 1.136(a)); sets shortened statutory period (SSP) and explains variable expiry rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes language about the shortened statutory period (typically three months), the two-month first-reply rule affecting variable expiry, and maximum six-month cap. Notes special cases where 37 CFR 1.136(a) is not available (e.g., reissue litigation, reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: When second/subsequent final rejection is improper (new grounds not necessitated by amendment or IDS-with-fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Second or any subsequent actions on the merits shall be final, except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant's amendment nor based on information submitted in an IDS filed during the 37 CFR 1.97(c) period with the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new grounds are introduced improperly, the next Office action should not be made final. See MPEP § 609.04(b). Also specific statutory amendments (e.g., to 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103) may affect finality rules; new grounds caused by such amendments have limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make final where new rejection is on prior art not of record for amended claims that should reasonably have been expected
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or subsequent action should not be made final if it includes a rejection, on prior art not of record, of any claim amended to include limitations which should reasonably have been expected to be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112 for incompleteness that could be answered by amendment — examiner should anticipate amendment and avoid making final. See MPEP § 904 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraphs 7.40 / 7.40.01 / 7.40.02 — Final when necessitated by amendment, IDS-with-fee, or joint research agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.40: Action Is Final, Necessitated by Amendment — applicant’s amendment necessitated the new ground(s) of rejection presented; ¶7.40.01: necessitated by IDS filed under 37 CFR 1.97(c) with fee; ¶7.40.02: necessitated by invoking joint research agreement prior art exclusion under 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each paragraph sets the action as final and contains SSP/extension notice; these form paragraphs should not be used in reissue litigation or reexamination proceedings where inapplicable. Bracketed fields require appropriate insertion of dates or descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-action final rejection in continuing/substitute applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of a new application may be finally rejected in the first Office action where (A) the new application is a continuing application of, or a substitute for, an earlier application, and (B) all claims are drawn to the same invention claimed in the earlier application and would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if entered earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make first-action final where the new application contains material presented in the earlier application after final rejection or closing of prosecution that required further consideration or raised new matter. Continuation-in-part with new subject matter precludes first-action final rejection. Use Form Paragraphs 7.41 / 7.41.03 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraphs 7.41 / 7.41.03 / 7.42.09 — Specific first-action final templates
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.41 Action Is Final, First Action — template for first-action final in continuation/substitute; ¶7.41.03 for CPA (37 CFR 1.53(d)); ¶7.42.09 for first action following RCE (37 CFR 1.114).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each paragraph requires insertion of appropriate bracketed material and is accompanied by SSP/extension language. Certain prerequisites (e.g., preceding form paragraphs) must be met for these templates to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prematureness of final rejection — practice and reviewability
rubrics_metrics.description: Any question as to prematureness of a final rejection should be raised while the application is still pending before the primary examiner; prematureness is a practice question and is reviewable by petition under 37 CFR 1.181 but not as a ground for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Premature finality is distinct from tenability of the rejection and must be addressed via petition while the application remains pending. See MPEP § 1002.02(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of finality when premature (Form ¶7.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the primary examiner finds the final rejection to have been premature on reconsideration, the finality of the rejection should be withdrawn while the application is still pending. The finality cannot be vacated once the application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42: 'Applicant’s request for reconsideration of the finality of the rejection of the last Office action is persuasive and, therefore, the finality of that action is withdrawn.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of final rejection — general grounds and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a non‑premature final rejection has been entered, it should not be withdrawn at applicant’s request except on a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b); the examiner may withdraw the rejection if new facts/reasons show the claims are allowable or patentable (including in reexamination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal to apply a new ground of rejection is permissible but limited: only where a new reference fully meets at least one claim or meets it except for differences shown to be completely obvious. Do not use withdrawal to apply subsidiary, cumulative, or merely better references. When withdrawn, amendments filed after final are ordinarily entered. New grounds after appeal require supervisory patent examiner approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for reply to a final rejection — variable SSP rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All final rejections setting a 3-month shortened statutory period (SSP) should contain form paragraph(s) advising that if a first reply is filed within 2 months, the SSP will expire 3 months from the mailing date or on the date the advisory action is mailed, whichever is later; in no event will the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from mailing date of the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 2-month first-reply deadline falls on a weekend/holiday, a reply filed on next business day is deemed within 2 months. The variable reply procedure does not apply to SSPs less than 3 months (e.g., some reissue litigation or reexamination cases). See MPEP § 710.05 for filing date computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory actions — examiner determinations after applicant first reply within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a final Office action sets a variable reply period and applicant files a complete first reply within 2 months, the examiner must determine if the reply: (1) places the application in condition for allowance; (2) places in condition for allowance except for matters of form which examiner can change; or (3) does not place the application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If (1) or (2), process as allowance and no extension fees due. If (3), the advisory action should inform applicant that the SSP for reply expires 3 months from the date of final rejection or mailing date of the advisory action (check PTOL-303 box 1.b). If applicant does not file a complete first reply within 2 months, examiner should check box 1.a on PTOL-303. The timing of advisory action mailing affects when SSP runs and extension fee calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendments and extension-fee consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files a complete first reply within 2 months of final action, an examiner’s amendment to place the application in condition for allowance may be made without payment of extension fees even if made more than 3 months from the final action (but not more than 6 months). If no complete first reply within 2 months, authorization to make an amendment to place application in condition for allowance must be made within the SSP or an extended period obtained with petition and fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner’s amendment correcting only formal matters identified after reply does not require an extension fee if reply already put the application in condition for allowance except for formal matters. Examiner’s amendment may not be made more than 6 months after the final action (application would be abandoned by operation of law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) — petition/fee and authorization by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) requires a petition for an extension and the appropriate fee provided in 37 CFR 1.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where extension is necessary to place application in condition for allowance, applicant may file petition & fee or give authorization to examiner to make the petition of record and charge a deposit account; authorizations must be of record before the extended period expires and must be made of record in an examiner’s amendment with name, date, deposit account number, length of extension requested and amount to be charged. Use Form Paragraph 13.02.02 for telephone authorization entries.
